content:
A security researcher has discovered that some of the world’s most popular websites were compromised in an attempt to steal cryptocurrency from iPhone users.

A total of 178 websites were affected, including BBC, CNN, HSBC, IKEA, and Zoom. Reasonably recent versions of iOS are safe, and so far it appears that only a few thousand dollars have been stolen …

Reuters reports that hackers attacked Optimizely, a website optimization platform used by many major websites.

Malicious JavaScript was aimed ​at visitors to the websites of 178 organizations ​across various sectors through Optimizely, according to researcher Scott Helme. The scripts attempted ​to replace cryptocurrency payment addresses with the attacker’s wallet, ​skim card numbers as users entered credit card details, steal cookies and screenshots, and plant exploit code on iOS devices. Cybersecurity firm ​HudsonRock also said it had found evidence that ​the sites had served malicious code to their visitors.

Several of the affected companies said that they have disabled the Optimizely scripts and are investigating potential impacts. Helme says almost all of the rogue code has now been removed, and that Apple patched iOS after an identical attack method was detected last month.

The Coruna loader is byte-identical to a sample we analysed in October from a different campaign. The kit’s own comments say iOS 18.7.3 and later, and 26.3 and later, are patched.

Helme monitored the attacker’s wallets and discovered that only $7,040 has been stolen, though it’s not possible to see how many payment card numbers were obtained.

As always, the best protection against this type of attack is to promptly update all your Apple devices to the latest OS versions they support.

  • Apple TV 4K (latest model)
  • Apple AirPods Pro 3
  • Apple HomeView
  • meross Smart Garage Door Opener
  • Logitech MX Master 4 for Mac
